correctness.rationale: For all positive F0,N0,mu,a,h,d,n, the local equilibrium exists uniquely by a positive loss derivative. Implicit differentiation gives P'/P = Q[n-(d-n)ahS]/[(1+ahS)J] with Q,J>0. When n<d, S decreases from S0 to 0, giving exactly one interior minimum iff ahS0>n/(d-n); other parameters give strictly increasing P. An exact source-to-R comparison yields sign[(1-e^{-nR})+(e^{-dR}-e^{-nR})ahS0]. The cutoff Y(R) increases strictly from n/(d-n) to infinity, proving exactly one returning radius if and only if there is an interior minimum, all equalities handled. An independently run standard-library checker passed 3614 finite supplemental assertions.

The 2008/2009 papers use broader mobile-predator PDEs but the full inspected results concern movement and recruitment shapes, not a theorem whose specialization implies this exact cutoff. The 2012 simulation model also lacks the required analytic implication.

originality.rationale: A focused equivalence and implication comparison with the complete original model and three relevant primary studies did not locate the exact unique survivorship trough plus finite-survey return-radius classification. The model, generic survival formulas and qualitative spatial recruitment classes are pre-existing. Historical priority is provisional rather than established by absence of search hits.
residual_risks: An unlocated historic treatment of this pre-existing equilibrium model may have independently stated the global one-minimum or exact return-radius identity.

The 2004 paper contains numerical classification over finite windows; detailed unpublished algebra or supplementary materials not captured in inspected published text could preempt historical priority.
The theorem does not extend to dynamic predator movement, other kernel families or physiological population dynamics.

value.rationale: Nathan and Casagrandi explicitly classify finite-window survival trends at a 95th-percentile seed radius using a tolerance; whether the same ecological site changes apparent survival direction when the survey radius is extended is mathematically and operationally motivated. The theorem supplies a sharp necessary/sufficient condition for a survival trough, proves unique eventual recovery, and identifies the unique exact return radius and source-intensity threshold. This is substantive structure beyond generic local curvature or numeric sampling. It provides an idealized interpretation benchmark, without forecasting field outcomes.
